body:
Hiring a senior freelance brand designer means buying one experienced person's judgment directly, without an agency account manager in between.

The trade-off is that you carry more of the coordination yourself, so the choice of designer matters more.

This list gives nine designers across eight countries, with where they are based, what they charge, how they work and links to their portfolios.

How I picked these designers

I started on Contra and Behance, the two platforms where independent designers publish their own profiles.

I only included solo freelancers, not studios, and only when I could open the profile and check the facts myself.

Some profiles use the word "senior" in the title, and others show years of experience or senior-level work instead, so I say which in each section.

This is not a ranking, and I have not worked with most of these designers.

Ratings, rates and prices are as shown on each profile on November 23, 2026, and they change often.

1. Arek Dvornechuck (Ebaqdesign), Brooklyn, New York, USA

I am first on this list, so you can see the standard I am measuring the others against.

I am a senior art director based in Brooklyn, New York, with over 20 years of experience.

I handle strategy, identity, websites and motion graphics myself, so you work directly with the designer doing the work, with no account managers or junior designers in between.

My pricing is a flat $3,000 per week for any design work, and there is no hourly billing.

A complete brand identity or rebrand, which I call the Brand Sprint, is delivered in one week for $3,000, with several logo concepts, a logo animation, colours, typography, brand guidelines, business cards and launch assets.

Bigger projects add weeks at the same rate, such as motion and launch assets in week two, website design in week three and development after that, and a month booked upfront is $10,000.

We agree the scope and number of weeks on the kickoff call, so the total price is fixed before work starts and revisions within that scope are included.

Recent clients include NextDimension AI, where I redesigned the identity and website, and the Sint Maarten law firm Fox Berman.

See my pricing and past work.

2. Sophie O'Connor, London, UK

Sophie describes herself as an independent, strategic brand designer, and she works from London.

Her Contra profile says she has 20 years of experience creating identities and design systems.

She pairs clean, minimalist design with strategic insight, and lists brand strategy, logo design, typography and web design among her skills.

Her projects include branding for BBC Studios Audio Productions, naming and identity for Shape & Sate, a visual identity for Mayhap Coffee, a rebrand for SOVAM and a website for Firebird Pictures.

She lists a Visual Identity Package at $8,000 and a Brand Identity Package at $10,000, and her hourly rate is $100 to $150.

Her profile shows a 5.0 rating from 2 reviews, and Contra marks her as a quick responder who replies within 24 hours.

She is a good fit when you want strategy and identity from the same person and a designer who has worked on media brands.

See Sophie's portfolio on Contra.

3. Sanja Planinic, New York, USA

Sanja is an independent, multidisciplinary designer and art director based in New York.

Her profile says she has over a decade of experience in branding, packaging and website design.

Contra lists her as a Top Independent, a badge it gives to top-rated freelancers, with more than $10k in verified earnings.

Packaging is a big part of her portfolio, with work such as Velvet, a visual identity and packaging project, and Amber Waves packaging.

Her other projects include visual identities for Barely and Glyph, The Bloody Mary Book and work for the 82nd Street Partnership.

She also builds websites and lists Framer, Webflow, Shopify, Squarespace and WordPress among her tools.

Her hourly rate is $100 to $150, and her Visual Identity and Website Design packages are priced on request.

She is a good fit for consumer brands that need packaging and a website from the same designer.

See Sanja's portfolio on Contra.

4. Ileana Pietragalli, Belén de Escobar, Argentina

Ileana is a senior designer based in Belén de Escobar, near Buenos Aires.

She has 28 years of experience across brand identity, digital products and visual communication, the longest on this list.

Her profile says she has led design for a New York financial services firm, founded and run her own creative agency in Buenos Aires and taught at the University of Buenos Aires.

She works across the full design process, from the first concept to production-ready files.

Her projects include the logo and illustrations for Bubblelicious, a bubble tea shop in Sweden, and the creative, design and event production for the launch of the Toyota 86 coupé at the Gálvez racing circuit in Buenos Aires.

She has also branded a real estate company, from stands and brochures to its website and app, and has a portfolio of financial branding work.

Her hourly rate is $25 to $50, which is among the lowest on this list for the most experience.

She speaks Spanish and English, and her time zone overlaps well with the US.

See Ileana's portfolio on Contra.

5. Arthur Lang, Berlin, Germany

Arthur is a senior designer based in Berlin.

His profile says he has over a decade of experience in branding, visual design and creative leadership.

He describes his strengths as building scalable design systems, leading cross-functional projects and streamlining workflows.

His best-documented project is a corporate identity redesign for Think-it, a company that connects North Africa's software engineers with global teams, built around diamonds and a vibrant blue.

His portfolio also includes a rebrand for kununu, the book design for Minor Cosmopolitan and a project called Fire Faísca Funke.

He speaks English, Portuguese and German, which helps if your brand has to work in several of those markets.

His hourly rate is $25 to $50.

See Arthur's portfolio on Contra.

6. Humberto Carrero, Barcelona, Spain

Humberto is a strategy-driven senior brand designer based in Barcelona.

He has over 10 years of experience working with companies and branding agencies around the world.

His process covers research, brand strategy, visual identity, brand guidelines, packaging, UI design, art direction and editorial design.

He says he can run full projects from scratch on his own or as part of a team, and that he has management experience.

His projects include a brand book for lool eyewear, East Drops and work for the Observatori contra l'homofòbia in Catalonia.

He lists a Brand design package at $5,000 and a Brand + Packaging package at $8,000, and his hourly rate is $50 to $75.

He works in English and Spanish, and he is a good fit for product brands that need packaging as well as an identity.

See Humberto's portfolio on Contra.

7. Gabriela Yanez, Mexico City, Mexico

Gabriela is an art director and brand identity expert based in Mexico City.

She has over 10 years of experience in the creative field.

She says she makes each task easy to understand and implement through organisation, teamwork and planning.

Contra lists her as a Top Independent with a 5.0 rating from 3 reviews.

Her published work is mostly event branding, for events such as Directors' Summit, Impact Week and Power Hour.

Her prices are among the clearest on this list: logo design at $1,050, brand identity design at $2,560 and a consultation at $130 an hour.

She works in English and Spanish, and she is a good fit for event and conference brands.

See her website and her work on Contra.

8. Dalibor Pajic, Auckland, New Zealand

Dalibor is a senior brand designer based in Auckland who builds identity systems for venture-backed companies.

He says he has more than 18 years of experience shaping identity systems for product-led and growth-stage companies.

He works between strategy and design, turning complex ideas into clear visuals that scale across brand and product, with a focus on clarity, structure and long-term coherence.

Most of his portfolio is tech logo design, such as Motif One, Accelera for developer tools and cloud infrastructure, Celestia and Nuclei, a biotech monogram.

One of his older marks, Hello Nature, was featured in LogoLounge 13.

He publishes six fixed packages, from a basic logo at $1,275 to a full brand identity system at $4,150, plus a 16-icon custom icon system at $2,200.

His hourly rate is $75 to $100, and his profile shows a 5.0 rating from 2 reviews and more than $5k in verified earnings.

He is a good fit for tech and AI startups that want a sharp mark and a system around it.

See Dalibor's portfolio on Contra.

9. Caro Visser, Cape Town, South Africa

Caro is a designer and art director based in Cape Town, and she calls herself an all-round creative.

She sums up her experience as "Food. Fashion. Flora.", and says she loves building visual languages and eye-catching work.

Her projects include a brand identity for a guest house, a brand and website for an eco-friendly honey company and the brand identity, packaging and website for The Spekboom Co.

She also lists web design, motion design and digital marketing among her skills.

Her packages are the most affordable on this list: Branding Basics at $300 and Bespoke Brand Architecture at $750, with an hourly rate of $25 to $50.

She is a good fit for small food, hospitality and lifestyle businesses on a tight budget.

See Caro's portfolio on Contra.

What to check before you hire a senior freelancer

Start with the work, not the title, because a senior label only tells you how long someone has been practising.

Look for finished identities with the full system, including guidelines, colours, type and applications.

Ask who will do the work, since a freelancer you meet is not always the person who sends the files.

Check the timeline in writing, and ask how many concepts you will see and how many rounds of revisions are included.

Compare the scope of each quote line by line, not just the total, because a $1,000 logo and a $10,000 identity are different products.

Is it better to hire one senior freelancer or a small studio?

For a focused identity with one clear decision-maker, one senior freelancer is usually the better choice.

You get one person's judgment from the first call to the final files, and the price is often lower than a studio's.

A small studio makes more sense when the brief spreads across several jobs, such as strategy research, a new website, motion and a team to run it.

Many freelancers are solo, so check how they handle peak workloads and which tasks they outsource.

If you want the freelancer's judgment with a team behind the work, ask whether they bring in other specialists and who manages them.

For a fuller comparison of cost and timing, read how a brand sprint compares with an agency and how long branding takes.

FAQ

faq.question: How much does a senior freelance brand designer cost?
faq.answer: Rates vary widely. The designers in this article list hourly rates from $25 to $150, and fixed packages from $300 for basic branding to $10,000 for a full brand identity. Compare what each price includes before deciding.

faq.question: Are these designers verified?
faq.answer: I checked each fact on the designer's own public profile. I have not verified their client work, and I have not hired most of them, so check their references before you commit.

faq.question: Should I choose a freelancer who lists "senior" in the title?
faq.answer: Use the title as a starting point, not a guarantee. Look at finished identities and ask for references from clients similar to yours.

faq.question: Can a freelancer handle a full brand, including the website?
faq.answer: Some can. Several designers here, including Sanja Planinic, Caro Visser and me, design websites as well as identities, so ask which parts they deliver themselves.
